text:
## PART 9: COMMON APPROVAL MISTAKES (Don't Make These!)  
❌ **Mistake 1:** Overlook recent late payments (weight of recent payment history)
✅ **Correct:** Weight recent activity (last 24 months) more heavily  
❌ **Mistake 2:** Accept stated income without verification
✅ **Correct:** Verify income with tax returns, W2s, employer letters  
❌ **Mistake 3:** Ignore DTI when credit score is excellent
✅ **Correct:** High DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score  
❌ **Mistake 4:** Approve at max LTV without strong credit and income
✅ **Correct:** Higher LTV requires stronger credit and income profile  
❌ **Mistake 5:** Waive conditions without clear authorization
✅ **Correct:** Conditions exist to reduce risk; document any waivers

raw_entities.name: Overlooking Recent Late Payments in Credit Assessment
raw_entities.description: A common approval error where recent late payments are not weighted appropriately in credit decisions. The finding highlights that recent payment activity (last 24 months) should be weighted more heavily than historical data to accurately assess current borrower risk.
context: Mistake 1: Overlook recent late payments (weight of recent payment history)
Correct: Weight recent activity (last 24 months) more heavily

raw_entities.name: Accepting Stated Income Without Verification
raw_entities.description: A critical control weakness where applicant income is accepted at face value without independent verification. The correct procedure requires verification through tax returns, W2s, or employer letters to validate income claims.
context: Mistake 2: Accept stated income without verification
Correct: Verify income with tax returns, W2s, employer letters

raw_entities.name: Ignoring Debt-to-Income Ratio When Credit Score is Excellent
raw_entities.description: A control deficiency where high debt-to-income ratios are overlooked because the applicant has an excellent credit score. The finding emphasizes that high DTI increases default risk independent of credit score performance.
context: Mistake 3: Ignore DTI when credit score is excellent
Correct: High DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score

raw_entities.name: Approving Maximum LTV Without Strong Credit and Income Profile
raw_entities.description: A risk control gap where maximum loan-to-value approvals are granted without corresponding strength in the applicant's credit and income profile. Higher LTV lending requires stronger underlying credit and income documentation to mitigate increased default risk.
context: Mistake 4: Approve at max LTV without strong credit and income
Correct: Higher LTV requires stronger credit and income profile

raw_entities.name: Waiving Approval Conditions Without Clear Authorization
raw_entities.description: A governance and control weakness where approval conditions are waived without documented authorization. The finding stresses that conditions exist to reduce risk and any waivers must be clearly documented and authorized.
context: Mistake 5: Waive conditions without clear authorization
Correct: Conditions exist to reduce risk; document any waivers

properties.name: Overlooking Recent Late Payments in Credit Assessment

properties.finding_summary: Auditors identified instances where recent late payments were not adequately weighted in credit decisions, contrary to sound underwriting practice
properties.evidence: Recent payment history (last 24 months) was not given appropriate weight in credit assessment decisions
properties.root_cause: Underwriting staff failed to prioritize recent payment activity in credit evaluation
properties.management_response: Weight recent activity (last 24 months) more heavily in credit assessment process

properties.finding_summary: Applicant income was accepted at face value without independent verification documentation
properties.evidence: Income stated by applicants was not corroborated with tax returns, W2s, or employer letters
properties.root_cause: Underwriting process did not enforce mandatory income verification requirements
properties.management_response: Verify all income with supporting documentation including tax returns, W2s, and employer letters

properties.name: Ignoring Debt-to-Income Ratio When Credit Score is Excellent

properties.affected_area: debt-to-income analysis and credit risk assessment
properties.finding_summary: Debt-to-income ratio was not adequately considered when applicants had excellent credit scores, creating unrecognized default risk
properties.evidence: High DTI ratios were overlooked in cases where credit scores were excellent
properties.root_cause: Over-reliance on credit score as sole indicator of creditworthiness, neglecting DTI as independent risk factor
properties.management_response: Evaluate DTI as a standalone risk factor; high DTI increases default risk regardless of credit score

properties.name: Approving Maximum LTV Without Strong Credit and Income Profile

properties.finding_summary: Maximum loan-to-value ratios were approved without corresponding strong credit and income profiles to support the elevated risk
properties.evidence: Approvals at maximum LTV were granted to applicants with weaker credit and income documentation
properties.root_cause: Underwriting controls did not enforce correlation between LTV approval levels and applicant credit/income strength
properties.management_response: Require stronger credit and income profiles to support higher LTV approvals

properties.name: Waiving Approval Conditions Without Clear Authorization

properties.affected_area: approval conditions and risk mitigation controls
properties.finding_summary: Approval conditions designed to reduce credit risk were waived without documented clear authorization
properties.evidence: Conditions were removed from loan approvals without proper authorization documentation
properties.root_cause: Lack of enforcement of authorization requirements for condition waivers; insufficient documentation of waiver rationale
properties.management_response: Document all condition waivers with clear authorization; maintain audit trail of waiver decisions and rationale

stated_prohibitions: Do not overlook recent late payments in credit assessment
Do not accept stated income without verification
Do not ignore debt-to-income ratio based on excellent credit score alone
Do not approve maximum LTV without strong credit and income profile
Do not waive approval conditions without clear authorization
controls_in_place: Weight recent payment activity (last 24 months) heavily in credit decisions
Verify income with tax returns, W2s, and employer letters
Evaluate debt-to-income ratio as independent risk factor
Correlate LTV approval levels with credit and income strength
Require documented authorization for all condition waivers
